samples.summary: unsetRangeStyleValues treats a missing key as agreement, so a cell that carries only some of the requested keys loses the rest
samples.evidence: The conflict scan is `if (cellValue !== undefined && cellValue !== value) return false;` (sheet.ts:4306-4310), but the removal is `omitStyleKeys(existing.s, keys)` — it strips *all* requested keys regardless of which ones the cell actually agreed about. changeDecimals calls it with `{dp, nf:'number'}` (sheet.ts:4208-4210). Scenario: A1 = `12` with `{dp:1, nf:'number'}`, B1 = `12` with `{nf:'number'}` only (no dp). Select A1:B1, press decrease → target 0 === valueDp 0, so unset `{dp:1, nf:'number'}` runs. B1's `nf` matches and its `dp` is undefined, so no conflict is detected; B1 then has both keys omitted and ends up with no style at all, changing its render from `12.00` to `12`. The same asymmetry applies to the col/row/sheet/patch layer checks (sheet.ts:4258-4285), where a layer holding only `nf` and no `dp` is silently accepted and then stripped. The added tests only cover the case where the other cell *disagrees* about a value (currency, dp:5), never the case where it holds a strict subset of the keys.

samples.summary: Zero-floor guard still keys off the active cell alone, so a selection whose active cell is unstyled never steps down at all
samples.evidence: `if (dp + delta < 0 && !explicitDp) return;` derives its decision entirely from `getActiveDecimalState()` (the active cell). The new test covers active-cell-explicit-at-zero, but the mirror case still aborts the whole selection: A1 empty/unstyled (dp = valueDp = 0, explicitDp = false) and B1 = `12.567` with `{dp:3, nf:'number'}`. Selecting A1:B1 with A1 active and pressing decrease returns immediately, so B1 never steps from 3 → 2 even though the user pressed the key on a selection that clearly has decimals to drop. This is the same class of bug the delta claims to fix, only reached from the non-explicit side.

samples.summary: Decrease-at-zero is no longer a no-op: it can now write nf:'number' onto a cell that was plain, changing its rendering
samples.evidence: Previously `if (target < 0) return;` made a decrease at zero write nothing. Now `target = Math.max(0, dp + delta)` falls through to `setRangeStyle(patch)` with `patch.nf = 'number'` whenever `!nf || nf === 'plain'` (sheet.ts:4215-4219). Case: A1 value `1.234` with an explicit `{dp:0, nf:'plain'}` (or `dp:0` inherited from a non-owned column layer, which makes the unset branch return false). explicitDp is true so the guard does not fire; target = 0; the unset is refused; the code writes `{dp:0, nf:'number'}`. `formatValue` returns the raw string for 'plain' but runs Intl for 'number' (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:116,124-130), so the display changes from `1.234` to `1` and gains grouping separators — from a keystroke that used to do nothing at the floor.

samples.summary: unsetRangeStyleValues returns true even when it removed nothing, so the caller reports success for a no-op
samples.evidence: The function returns `true` unconditionally after the batch (sheet.ts:4385) without tracking whether any layer or cell edit actually occurred. If the requested key is not held by any owned layer and no scanned cell carries it (e.g. the holder is a merged-cell anchor that normalizes outside `targets`, or a cell not returned by `store.getGrid`), the function writes nothing and still reports success; `changeDecimals` then returns at sheet.ts:4211 and the decimal step silently does nothing. Tracking 'did I actually remove something' and returning false otherwise would let the caller fall back to the explicit write.

samples.summary: Object.entries keeps keys whose value is undefined, turning them into an impossible-to-satisfy conflict predicate
samples.evidence: `const entries = Object.entries(style)` (sheet.ts:4239) does not filter out explicitly-undefined values, unlike `normalizeStylePatch` used elsewhere (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/range-styles.ts:14-28). A caller passing `{dp: undefined}` (easy for a `Partial<CellStyle>` built from optional fields) yields an entry with `value === undefined`; every cell or layer that actually sets `dp` then trips `cellValue !== value` and the whole operation is refused, while `entries.length === 0` early-return never fires. The current single caller happens to pass concrete values, so this is latent rather than live.

mergedFrom.summary: unsetRangeStyleValues returns true even when it removed nothing, so the caller reports success for a no-op
mergedFrom.evidence: The function returns `true` unconditionally after the batch (sheet.ts:4385) without tracking whether any layer or cell edit actually occurred. If the requested key is not held by any owned layer and no scanned cell carries it (e.g. the holder is a merged-cell anchor that normalizes outside `targets`, or a cell not returned by `store.getGrid`), the function writes nothing and still reports success; `changeDecimals` then returns at sheet.ts:4211 and the decimal step silently does nothing. verdict.reason: The code is present as described. sheet.ts:4306-4310 treats an absent key on a cell as agreement (`cellValue !== undefined && cellValue !== value`), while sheet.ts:4312 removes ALL requested keys via omitStyleKeys (range-styles.ts:64-76), which deletes every key in the list unconditionally. changeDecimals (sheet.ts:4208-4210) supplies the pair {dp, nf:'number'}, so a selection-mate holding only {nf:'number'} (no dp) passes the conflict scan and then loses nf entirely. Because format.ts:111-113 returns the raw value when nf is absent and format.ts:119-131 renders 2 decimals for nf:'number' with no dp, such a cell (e.g. value 12.567 displaying 12.57) becomes unstyled and renders 12.567 — MORE decimals after pressing decrease — with the user-chosen number format silently destroyed. The refused/setRangeStyle path (sheet.ts:4215-4219) would instead write {dp:0} and keep nf, so the two paths diverge in stored state and in later rendering. The same undefined-means-agreement asymmetry exists in the layer scans (sheet.ts:4259, 4264, 4272, 4280) versus the strip-all writes (4322, 4333, 4345, 4357). This directly contradicts the method's own documented contract at sheet.ts:4228-4231 ("anything else within the selection ... refuses the whole operation rather than being flattened into it"), which the tests at decimals.test.ts:177-205 enforce for currency/percent; the subset case is untested (decimals.test.ts:207-224 only covers a disagreeing dp:5). No guard elsewhere prevents this: unsetRangeStyleValues has exactly one call site (sheet.ts:4210), and that call site is what supplies the two-key request. Real, reachable, in-lane silent state loss / wrong behavior — major.

verdict.reason: The guard exists as quoted (sheet.ts:4197), but the finding's claimed defect does not hold under this lens. (1) The stated expected outcome — B1 stepping 3 → 2 — is impossible in this API: changeDecimals computes ONE target from the active cell (sheet.ts:4202) and applies it uniformly via setRangeStyle (sheet.ts:4215-4219). Existing tests pin this: decimals.test.ts:104-117 drives B1 from dp:3 to dp:0, and decimals.test.ts:207-224 drives B1 from dp:5 to dp:0. So without the early return the mirror case would write {dp:0, nf:'number'} to the whole selection — B1 3 → 0, plus the exact zero-decimal residue on the unstyled active cell that this change exists to remove — not 3 → 2. (2) The resulting no-op is an explicitly documented, intentional tradeoff: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:240-243 ("A selection whose *other* cells still have decimals is then also left alone") and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:87-89 list it verbatim under "Known deviations". (3) Under the Correctness rubric there is no crash, no null/undefined deref, no data loss or overwrite, no async/ordering fault and no broken invariant — the path writes nothing at all. What is left is a product/design decision about active-cell-driven selection semantics (per-cell stepping is not a capability anywhere in this API), which belongs to the design-fit lens, not correctness.

finding.summary: Unsetting `nf` across the whole selection destroys other cells' number formats (currency/date/percent)
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` derives `keys = nf === 'number' ? ['dp','nf'] : ['dp']` from the ACTIVE cell only (sheet.ts:4196-4207), then `unsetRangeStyleKeys(keys)` deletes those keys from every owned layer and from `cell.s` of every cell in the selection (sheet.ts:4315-4335, removeCellStyleKeysInRange 4343-4372). Example: select A1:B1 where A1 = '1.5' with cell style {nf:'number', dp:2} (active) and B1 has {nf:'currency', cu:'USD', dp:2}. Decrease decimals: target 1 === valueDp(A1) 1 and nf==='number', so keys=['dp','nf']; the ownership guard (4242-4277) only rejects layers OUTSIDE the selection, so B1's own cell style is stripped and B1 silently loses its currency format (same for a 'date'-formatted neighbour stamped by setData). A key set chosen from one cell must not be unset from cells that never had that format.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `changeDecimals` does not call `unsetRangeStyleKeys(keys)`; that function does not exist in packages/sheets/src at all (grep finds it only in docs and .agent-review text). Instead, sheet.ts:4208-4210 builds a key/VALUE map (`nf === 'number' ? { dp, nf } : { dp }`) and calls `unsetRangeStyleValues`, which is value-aware and all-or-nothing: the layer checks at 4257-4286 abort on any disagreeing value including layers inside the selection, and the pre-write cell scan at 4292-4317 returns false (before any store write, which begins at 4319) for any cell whose own style holds a different value: `if (cellValue !== undefined && cellValue !== value) return false;` (4307-4310). In the reviewer's own example, B1's `nf === 'currency' !== 'number'` triggers that early return, nothing is written, and `changeDecimals` falls through to `setRangeStyle({dp: target})` (4215-4219), so B1 keeps `nf: 'currency'`/`cu: 'USD'`. The scenario is additionally covered by existing tests at decimals.test.ts:177-193 and 195-205.

finding.summary: Decrease/increase decimals can change other cells' displayed precision because the unset decision uses only the active cell's `valueDp`
finding.evidence: `const { dp, nf, valueDp, explicitDp } = await this.getActiveDecimalState()` (4196) and `if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable)` (4203) test the ACTIVE cell's raw-value precision but the resulting unset applies to the whole selection. Concretely: A1='1.5', A2='1.2345', select A1:A2. Decrease → writes {dp:0, nf:'number'} for both (shows 2 / 1). Increase → dp=0 explicit, target 1 === valueDp(A1)=1, nf='number' → all dp/nf removed → A1 renders '1.5' (intended) but A2 jumps back to '1.2345', i.e. pressing *increase by one decimal* moved A2 from 0 to 4 decimals. The old code wrote an explicit uniform dp and had no such divergence.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists exactly as described: getActiveDecimalState (sheet.ts:4165-4186) derives valueDp/explicitDp from this.activeCell alone, changeDecimals destructures it at 4196 and gates the unset at 4205 on `target === valueDp`, yet unsetRangeStyleValues (4238-4249) applies to every range in the selection. Tracing A1='1.5', A2='1.2345' with A1:A2 selected: decrease writes {dp:0, nf:'number'} for both (4215-4219, explicitDp=false skips the unset); increase then sees dp=0/explicitDp=true/valueDp=1 and target=1, inheritable because nf==='number' (4204), so the unset removes dp and nf across the selection (4353-4380, returns true at 4385) and A2 reverts to raw-value rendering at 4 decimals — a one-step 'increase decimals' moving a non-active cell from 0 to 4 displayed decimals. The value-agreement guards inside unsetRangeStyleValues (4257-4311) do not fire because the whole selection holds the identical {dp:0, nf:'number'}, and both callers (view/spreadsheet.ts:536,546) pass multi-cell selections through unchanged. Real, in-lane wrong-behavior bug for heterogeneous selections; no test covers it.

finding.summary: Comment/assumption that dropping `nf:'number'` keeps the cell looking the same is false — grouping separators are lost
finding.evidence: Lines 4204-4207 justify removing `nf` with "the cell keeps looking the same", but `formatValue(value,'number',dp)` goes through `toLocaleString` (format.ts:127-130) which adds thousands separators, while plain format returns the raw string verbatim (format.ts:111-113). For value '1234.5': with {nf:'number',dp:1} the cell shows '1,234.5'; after the unset it shows '1234.5'. The new test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:89-92 encodes exactly this lossy outcome (`toBe('1234.5')`). So decrease-then-increase on a number-formatted cell silently drops the user's number format and its grouping.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: sheet.ts:4204-4212 unsets both `dp` and `nf` when `nf === 'number'` and `target === valueDp`, justified by a comment claiming the cell "keeps looking the same". That is false in the grouping dimension: format.ts:111-113 returns the raw string for plain/undefined, while format.ts:124-131 routes 'number' through safeFormat -> toLocaleString (format.ts:9-19) with default grouping, and toDisplayString (sheet.ts:962-969) uses formatValue with the effective nf/dp. So '1234.5' renders '1,234.5' with {nf:'number',dp:1} and '1234.5' once unset — exactly what the new test asserts (decimals.test.ts:89-92). Beyond the plain-cell round trip (which is intentional), a reachable path drops a user-chosen format: value '1234' with {nf:'number',dp:1} (via setRangeStyle({nf:'number'}) then changeDecimals(-1)) then changeDecimals(-1) gives target 0 === valueDp 0, so unsetRangeStyleValues({dp:1,nf:'number'}) matches and strips both, changing display from '1,234.0' to '1234' and silently discarding the user's number format. The existing test decimals.test.ts:156-175 does not cover this because valueDp(0) !== target(2) there, so the branch never fires. The `nf === 'number'` condition cannot distinguish a format changeDecimals synthesized from one the user set, so the guard is under-specified — a real logic/state-loss bug, major.

finding.summary: `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` rewrites cells through `compactCell`, dropping spill metadata
finding.evidence: `const nextCell = compactCell(existing, next); ... await this.store.set(anchor, nextCell)` (4366-4370). `compactCell` copies only `v`, `f` and `s` (style-mutation.ts:57-69), while `Cell` also carries `spillRows`, `spillCols`, `spillAnchor` and `spillBlocked` (model/core/types.ts:209-217). Decreasing decimals over a spill anchor or a spilled ghost cell that happens to carry a style therefore erases its spill bookkeeping, corrupting spill rendering/blocking state. The same lossy pattern exists in `clearCellStylesInRange`/`setStyle`, so it is pre-existing, but this change adds a new user-reachable path to it.

verdict.reason: The described lossy rewrite is present, only misnamed/misnumbered by the reviewer: it lives in `unsetRangeStyleValues` at sheet.ts:4373-4379 (`const nextCell = compactCell(cell, nextStyle); ... await this.store.set(anchor, nextCell)`), fed by cellEdits that carry the full existing cell (sheet.ts:4302-4315). `compactCell` copies only `v`, `f`, `s` (style-mutation.ts:57-69), while `Cell` also persists `spillRows`/`spillCols`/`spillAnchor`/`spillBlocked` (types.ts:209-217), and `store.set` wholesale replaces the stored cell (store/memory.ts:97-100), so those fields are erased rather than merged. The path is user-reachable: `changeDecimals` calls `unsetRangeStyleValues({dp})` when a decrease restores inheritance (sheet.ts:4205-4212), and spill anchors are persisted with a style (`calculator.ts:136` writes `{v, f, s: style, spillRows, spillCols}`), so they pass the `existing?.s` filter at sheet.ts:4303 and get rewritten without spill fields. The calculator then never clears the ghosts because of `if (cell.spillRows && cell.spillCols && !cell.spillBlocked)` (calculator.ts:74-80), leaving orphaned ghost cells and broken spill/blocking state — a real data-integrity/invariant bug in the correctness lane. Ghost cells alone are indeed shielded by the `!existing?.s` guard (they are written with only `v`/`spillAnchor`, calculator.ts:141), and the pattern is pre-existing in setStyle (sheet.ts:3682), but neither fact makes the anchor path non-blocking.
